findings.evidence: Physlib supplies the pieces: `LorentzGroup.smul_timeComponent_eq_toVector_minkowskiProduct Λ v : (Λ • v).timeComponent = ⟪toVector Λ⁻¹, v⟫ₘ` (upstream/Physlib/.../LorentzGroup/ToVector.lean:93), `isOrthochronous_inv_iff` and `orthochronoustoVelocity` (Orthochronous/Basic.lean:48,63), `Lorentz.Velocity.norm_spatialPart_le_timeComponent` (Velocity/Basic.lean:59), `minkowskiProduct_eq_timeComponent_spatialPart` (MinkowskiProduct.lean:156), plus the PR's own `norm_le_onShellEnergy` (MassShell.lean:86); `isOrthochronous_of_restricted` (Restricted/Basic.lean:47) covers rotations and generalized boosts.
findings.fix: State `theorem timeComponent_smul_onShellMomentum_nonneg {Λ : LorentzGroup d} (hΛ : IsOrthochronous Λ) (m) (p) : 0 ≤ (Λ • onShellMomentum m p).timeComponent` and derive both current lemmas (boost: 00-entry `γ β > 0` via the PR's `γ_pos`; rotation: 00-entry `= 1`). Then `massShellAction_mul`, `onShellMomentum_massShellAction_boost` and `..._rotation` all follow for every orthochronous — hence every restricted — `Λ` with no per-generator work.
findings.issue: `timeComponent_boost_smul_onShellMomentum_nonneg` (line 248) and `timeComponent_rotation_smul_onShellMomentum_nonneg` (line 283) are two generator-specific proofs of one fact: an orthochronous `Λ` keeps the energy of an on-shell momentum non-negative. This is the hypothesis `massShellAction_mul` (line 208) and `onShellMomentum_massShellAction` (line 195) need, and the PR description names supplying it for the whole restricted group as the remaining milestone step.

findings.evidence: Line 49 extracts only `((mem_rotations_iff _).1 Λ.2).1`; the rest descend from `toVector_rotation`, which Physlib proves from the 00-entry alone (upstream/Physlib/.../LorentzGroup/Rotations.lean:189-192 via `toVector_eq_basis_iff_timeComponent_eq_one`). `Rotations` carries `IsProper` as a separate conjunct (Rotations.lean:24). Physlib's own precedent states this at the entry level, not via the subgroup (ToVector.lean:70).
findings.fix: State these five lemmas with hypothesis `(hΛ : Λ.1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) = 1)` on a plain `Λ : LorentzGroup d`; call sites with `Λ : Rotations d` pass `((mem_rotations_iff _).1 Λ.2).1`. The def `Rotations.toLinearIsometryEquiv` may stay keyed on `Rotations d` since Physlib offers no O(d) handle.
findings.issue: `Rotations d` bundles `IsProper` (det = 1), but none of `rotation_inr_inl_eq_zero` (34), `rotation_inl_inr_eq_zero` (40), `timeComponent_rotation_smul` (47), `spatialPart_rotation_smul_apply` (53) or `norm_spatialPart_rotation_smul` (60) uses it; they hold for every `Λ : LorentzGroup d` with `Λ.1 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inl 0) = 1`, i.e. for all spatial reflections too. The restriction propagates to `massShellAction_rotation` and `measurePreserving_massShellAction_rotation`, which are likewise true for improper spatial orthogonal maps.

findings.evidence: `onShellEnergy m p = √(m² + ‖p‖²) > 0 ↔ m ≠ 0 ∨ p ≠ 0` (line 60); the file proves both directions separately at lines 71 and 76, so the hypothesis as written splits a single general statement.
findings.fix: Replace `(hp : p ≠ 0)` by `(hE : 0 < onShellEnergy m p)`: for `p = 0` the left side is `0 < E`, otherwise the current argument applies. The present form is then `abs_mul_apply_lt_onShellEnergy hβ (onShellEnergy_pos_of_momentum_ne_zero m hp) i`, and strict positivity of the boosted energy `γ (E − β pᵢ)` becomes available for massive particles everywhere.
findings.issue: `abs_mul_apply_lt_onShellEnergy` assumes `p ≠ 0`, which is stronger than needed: `|β pᵢ| < E` holds whenever `0 < onShellEnergy m p`, in particular for a massive particle at zero momentum — the case the file's own `onShellEnergy_pos_of_mass_ne_zero` (line 71) covers and this lemma then cannot serve.

findings.evidence: Grep for `massShellAction_rotation_apply` over `code/` returns only its own definition (MassShell.lean:297) and no call site; `spatialPart_rotation_smul_apply` (RotationsExtensions.lean:53) already supplies the entry-sum form.
findings.fix: Drop it, or derive it in one `rw` chain from `massShellAction_rotation`, `Rotations.toLinearIsometryEquiv_apply`, `spatialPart_rotation_smul_apply` and `spatialPart_ofSpatialComponent`.
findings.issue: `massShellAction_rotation_apply` restates, at component level and by an independent route through `massShellAction_apply`, what `massShellAction_rotation` (line 304) already gives in general; it has no use in the PR.

summary: Three statements sit below their natural level: the two energy-non-negativity lemmas are generator-specific instances of one orthochronous fact (which is exactly what the remaining roadmap step needs), the rotation block lemmas never use the determinant condition bundled into `Rotations`, and the strict momentum bound assumes `p ≠ 0` where positivity of the energy suffices. One rotation lemma is also a second statement of a fact already proved in general in the same file.
